recognize_zh: 中央一顆單核球（monocyte）胞質內含一顆完整紅血球並伴空泡，即紅血球吞噬（erythrophagocytosis）；背景紅血球成團聚集，提示冷凝集素造成的自體免疫溶血。
features: Monocyte/macrophage with vacuolated grey-blue cytoplasm containing an intact engulfed red cell
Irregular clumps of overlapping red cells consistent with RBC agglutination
Many crenated red cells (echinocytes), likely drying/storage artifact
Band and segmented neutrophils without toxic change; a small lymphocyte adjacent to the phagocyte
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows red cells arranged in irregular clumps suggestive of agglutination, with numerous crenated forms that likely reflect artifact. A monocyte with vacuolated cytoplasm contains an intact phagocytosed erythrocyte. Accompanying neutrophils and a lymphocyte are morphologically unremarkable, and platelets are present. Erythrophagocytosis in blood, together with red cell agglutination, is consistent with antibody-mediated hemolysis such as cold agglutinin disease; correlation with direct antiglobulin test (C3d) and cold agglutinin titer is recommended.

ddx.vs: Rouleaux are linear stacks of red cells like coins, whereas agglutination forms irregular three-dimensional clumps that disperse on warming in cold agglutinin disease.
Warm AIHA typically shows prominent microspherocytes with IgG-positive DAT rather than cold-reactive agglutinates with C3d-only DAT.
HLH is diagnosed on marrow/tissue with activated histiocytes engulfing multiple cell lineages and clinical criteria, not a single erythrophagocytic monocyte with agglutination in blood.
PCH can also show erythrophagocytosis by neutrophils but is identified by a biphasic Donath-Landsteiner IgG antibody rather than IgM cold agglutinins.
